name: github work-item complete-unit foundation
$limitation: This plan pins the neutral semantic work-item manifest and earlier foundation seams. It does not by itself prove CHAOS-3606 activation, single-writer admission, runtime configuration, collector behavior, effects, or alias completion; those have their own plans and focused gates.

mutations.find:
{Name: "ai_attribution", GitHubEffect: true, LinearExpiredLeaseRetry: true},
	{Name: "estimate_coverage_metrics_daily", GitHubEffect: true, LinearExpiredLeaseRetry: true},
mutations.rationale: the GitHub Python work-item unit conditionally writes AI attribution beside the raw and derived work-item effects, so the neutral semantic manifest must retain it for atomic ownership
a misspelled or future family flag must not silently terminalize a unit whose per-alias watermark identities Go cannot prove
a collapsed canonical claim with no enabled alias has no authoritative watermark target and cannot be reported successful
successful completion of the one canonical crawl must advance every enabled family alias rather than only the canonical work-items watermark
the canonical unit result must retain the enabled alias identities for operational audit and compute checkpoint provenance

mutations.find:
var milestone githubMilestonePayload
	decoder := json.NewDecoder(bytes.NewReader(raw))
	decoder.UseNumber()
mutations.rationale: GitHub database identifiers above 2^53 must never pass through float64 before becoming the stable sprint identity. Anchor narrowed to the MILESTONE decoder: a second UseNumber() now exists on the comment path, and the bare anchor matched both -- mutating an unrelated site this entry never claimed to cover.
the normalized GitHub issue identity must retain its provider number so updates and derived metrics converge on the Python row

Python enriches every GitHub issue WorkItem with priority and service class before adding it to the provider batch. Anchor narrowed to the ISSUE path (its rationale and proof name issues): the pull-request normalizer grew an identical call, and the bare anchor matched both.

the Go composite must structurally account for every semantic list the real Python GitHub provider can emit, including conditional AI attribution -- and for NO others, since the proof compares the reflected field list against the seven families by ordered DeepEqual. Re-authored: this entry previously DELETED the AIAttributions field, which breaks the build at eight call sites, so no test ran and it scored INVALID -- reading as coverage while measuring nothing. Deletion cannot be the operator here, because no compiling mutation can remove a field other code references. Adding an undeclared eighth family is the compiling mutation that reaches the same assertion: the family list is pinned exactly, by name, order and count.
Python retains full provider timestamp precision in the semantic WorkItem and Sprint dataclasses; only the later ClickHouse projection may coerce to DateTime64(3)

mutations.find:
reopen_events = [
                replace(event, org_id=org_id) if hasattr(event, "org_id") else event
                for event in reopen_events
            ]
mutations.rationale: reopen rows are written to an org-partitioned ClickHouse table and must not retain the dataclass default empty tenant key

mutations.find:
interactions = [
                replace(event, org_id=org_id) if hasattr(event, "org_id") else event
                for event in interactions
            ]
mutations.rationale: comment interaction rows are tenant-partitioned and must be visible only under the owning organization

mutations.find:
sprints = [
                replace(sprint, org_id=org_id) if hasattr(sprint, "org_id") else sprint
                for sprint in sprints
            ]
mutations.rationale: milestone-derived sprint rows use org_id in their deduplication key and must be stamped before the sink write
